title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
gist: A Microsoft Research intern built a physics-informed ML pipeline that turns L1 solar-wind data into location-specific geomagnetically induced current risk for 66,935 U.S. substations, detecting nearly 80% of major space-weather events with 30-60 minutes of warning; operational use still requires utility validation.

insights.claim: Extreme space-weather events can induce currents in transmission networks that damage equipment and raise operational risk, and the key challenge is predicting when and where effects will be most severe with enough warning.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Geomagnetic storms are a tail risk for utilities and grid equipment suppliers.
insights.quote: The challenge is not only knowing that a storm is approaching, but estimating when and where its effects could be most severe
insights.locator: Forecasting a threat to critical infrastructure

insights.claim: The May 2024 geomagnetic storm degraded GPS accuracy and satellite operations, impacting farm operations in North America and Europe, while utilities across North America prepared for possible impacts.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Shows space weather already causes real economic disruption beyond the grid.

insights.claim: Regions with resistive bedrock can experience stronger geomagnetically induced currents than regions with conductive geology, and line orientation and latitude further shape asset exposure.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Grid GIC risk is highly location-specific, favoring granular rather than blanket hedging.

insights.claim: The pipeline forecasts space-weather risk 30-60 minutes ahead for 66,935 continental U.S. substations by combining solar-wind observations, AE and Dst index forecasts, physics-informed constraints, geological conductivity and grid data.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Demonstrates feasible substation-level hazard forecasting for grid operators.

insights.claim: The system works in three stages: L1 solar-wind data forecast AE and Dst indices, a gradient-boosting model estimates dB/dt per substation, and outputs are aggregated into a continental risk assessment.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Relatively lightweight ML (gradient boosting) suffices for actionable infrastructure forecasting.

insights.claim: A system of 50 AI agents helped explore features, validation strategies and model configurations across the pipeline.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Example of agentic AI accelerating applied ML research workflows, even for an intern project.
insights.quote: A system of 50 AI agents helped explore features, validation strategies, and model configurations across the pipeline.

insights.claim: The pipeline used only public data, including NASA OMNI, Kyoto World Data Center data, INTERMAGNET and USGS magnetometer observations, and GridSFM-derived grid data.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Public-data reproducibility lowers barriers for competitors and utilities to build similar tools.

insights.claim: Inference for all 66,935 substations took approximately 333 milliseconds, allowing many storm scenarios to be evaluated quickly.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Near-instant inference enables real-time scenario analysis in grid operations.
insights.quote: The current pipeline produced estimates for all 66,935 substations in approximately 333 milliseconds during measured inference

insights.claim: Over 2020-2026, the AE predictor achieved 410.2 nT RMSE, beating empirical and solar-wind-only baselines, while the Dst predictor achieved 7.2 nT RMSE and beat the Burton equation on 62.2% of peak-activity hours.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: ML beats legacy physics-empirical baselines in space-weather index forecasting.

insights.claim: Adding the Dst forecast to AE improved severe-event detection in the end-to-end system by 1.2 percentage points.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Shows incremental value of combining multiple geomagnetic signals.

insights.claim: The GIC risk stage detected 76.5% of major (≥10 nT/min), 81.2% of severe (≥20 nT/min) and 64.1% of extreme (≥50 nT/min) events, with the pipeline detecting nearly 80% of major space-weather events overall.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Meaningful but imperfect detection of extreme events leaves residual tail risk.
insights.locator: The GIC risk stage was evaluated differently

insights.claim: False-alarm rates rose with storm severity and detection was highest at northern stations where geomagnetic activity is strongest.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Operators face a missed-event versus false-alarm trade-off that affects adoption economics.
insights.locator: The GIC risk stage was evaluated differently

insights.claim: No widely deployed operational system provides a direct industry benchmark for substation-level GIC risk calculation, so the model was compared only against linear regression.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Signals a gap in the market for operational GIC forecasting tools.
insights.quote: There is no equivalent widely deployed operational system that provides a direct industry benchmark for this calculation
insights.locator: The GIC risk stage was evaluated differently

insights.claim: Location-specific early warnings could help utilities prioritize engineering review and take targeted actions such as adjusting reactive-power reserves or temporarily reconfiguring parts of the network.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Could reduce equipment damage costs and improve grid resilience spending efficiency.

insights.claim: Further validation with utilities and operational data is needed before the system could be used in grid operations.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Not deployment-ready; commercial impact is still distant.
insights.quote: Further validation with utilities and operational data would be needed before the system could be used in grid operations.

insights.claim: Planned next steps include temporal-transformer models to extend beyond the 30-60 minute window, international scaling, integration with grid operations workflows, and transformer-level asset risk.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Transformer-level granularity would make the tool relevant to asset insurance and equipment replacement planning.

insights.claim: The work connects to Microsoft Research's broader AI-for-power-systems effort, including GridSFM which applies deep learning to AC optimal power flow, pointing toward planning workflows that combine hazard forecasts, grid topology and power-flow analysis.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Microsoft is building a portfolio of grid AI tools, a possible future utility software play.
